units.translation: 6 Stephanus of Byzantium, Κτιμένη: a city of Thessaly given by Peleus to Phoenix, whose citizens Homer calls Dolopes . . . and 〈Apollonius〉 ‘Κτιμένην Δολοπηίδα’. cf. W 92
69. From Opus: Opus is a city of Locris, named after Opus the Elean. Homer (Iliad 2.531): ‘who dwelt in Cynus and Opus and Calliarus.’
9 Stephanus of Byzantium, Ὀπόεις | sch. 1776/81 e | 14 Hyginus, Fabulae 14 (48, 20 Schm.)

71-74. Mighty Eribotes: strong; it is formed by derivation from ἀλκή (strength), as φωνήεις from φωνή (voice). But Herodorus in his Argonautica (31 F 5 J.) calls him Eurybates and says he was the son of Teleon. The sons of Actor were Menoetius and Irus, and their sons were, of Menoetius and Sthenele, Patroclus, and of Irus, Eurytion.
13 καὶ τιμήεις παρὰ τὴν τιμήν added after φωνήν by A. cf. W 29 | 16 Μ. μὲν καὶ Σθενέλης Π. W : Μ. μὲν Π. in the manuscripts at this point, Μ. δὲ καὶ Σθενέλης Π. in the same manuscripts after sch. 69
75-76. And to rush upon: meaning to pursue. The word μετόπισθεν (behind) is redundant, and the conjunction καί is missing: ‘and when they should rout the ranks, he would turn them to flight.’
19 κλίνειαν W : -ειε L : -ει P (-η V) : -ωσι AF. Oileus puts the enemy to flight even when they already seem to be victorious | 20 τρέψειαν F, -ωσι A
77-78. Canthus went: Cleon also lists Canthus.
He is the son of Canethus, after whom the mountain in Boeotia is named; and he was the son of Abas, after whom the Euboeans are called Abantes.

81-82. To be destroyed: here δηωθῆναι is used in a rather novel sense for ‘to be ruined.’ The poet, as if grieving over the destruction of the heroes, exclaims in sequence: ‘as not for mortals.’ The sense is: there is no greatest evil which a man fails to encounter. Therefore it should be ἀπαυρεῖν with long alpha. Or: because no evil is greatest which would be grievous for men to experience, that is, to meet with.

83-85. Settings and risings: he says they are as far removed from the land of the Colchians as the settings are distant from the risings, since Libya is in the west and Colchis in the east.
13 καὶ added after ἐπεὶ by L

87. Guardians of Oechalia: children of Antiope. Of Oechalia in Euboea. For the younger poets say it is in Euboea, but Homer lists Oechalia in Pelasgian Argos (Iliad 2.730): ‘who held Oechalia, city of Eurytus the Oechalian,’ but others say it is a city of the same name.
